text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- No cover-up, Chretien says: PM denies Somalia commission finding that efforts were made to conceal wrongdoing.
- Ontario urged to put child first: Report proposes sweeping changes.
- NATO expansion a numbers game: European countries upset over U.S. stand to admit only three new members.
- Officer spared jail in Ipperwash slaying: OPP sergeant can't use gun for two years.
- China starts wooing Taiwan: Hong Kong a go-between in bid to coax island back into fold.
- Universities give recruitment old college try: Stealing a leaf from U.S. schools, Canada's postsecondary institutions are using business techniques to lure new students to their campuses.
- Baillie tied to Scotiabank deal: Ottawa's point man on financial sector mergers played role in National Trust takeover.
- Lockheed, Northrop strike C$11-billion deal: Likely the last big U.S. defence merger.
- Organized labor lures growing number of youth: Stuck in low-wage jobs, young workers are turning to unions for help.
- Law firm launches insurance suits for C$2 billion: Comes as Sun Life settles class actions.
- North American markets surge to new highs.
- Gold crashes to 12-year low: News that Australia has been unloading bullion in a big way sparks market rout; analysts predict the price collapse still has some way to run.
- Philip bids C$82 million for Intermetco: Dissidents win as Hamilton waste recycling firms tie knot.
